verses.1: The vision that the prophet Habakkuk saw:
verses.2: How long, LORD, will I cry for help and you not hear? I call to you, “Violence!” and you do not rescue.
verses.3: Why do you show me injustice, and make me watch oppression? Why do I see strife and quarrels advancing?
verses.4: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and judgment never goes forward, for the wicked surround the righteous — therefore judgment comes out perverted.
verses.5: Look among the nations and see — wonder and be astonished, for I am doing a work in your days that you will not believe, even if someone tells it to you.
verses.6: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that fierce and impetuous nation, who march through the breadth of the earth to seize homes not their own.
verses.7: Terror and dread go with them; their judgment comes from themselves, and their honor rises from their own strength.
verses.8: Their horses are swifter than leopards, and fiercer than evening wolves. Their horsemen spread out, and they fly like an eagle that pounces to eat.
verses.9: All of them come for violence — their faces are turned forward, and they gather captives like sand.
verses.10: He scoffs at kings and mocks rulers. He laughs at every fortress, and heaps up dust and captures it.
verses.11: Then the wind passes through and they go by, and their might is their god.
verses.12: Are you not from eternity, O LORD my God, my Holy One? You will not die. You have established judgment, and laid the foundation as a rock for argument.
verses.13: Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and you cannot bear to see oppression. Why then do you look with silence as the wicked swallow up the righteous?
verses.14: You make humans like the fish of the sea, like a creeping thing that has no ruler.
verses.15: They lift everything in a hook, drag it in a net, and gather it in their dragnet.
verses.16: Therefore they rejoice and are glad in their hearts — therefore they offer sacrifice to their net and pour out drink offerings to their dragnet, for in them their portion is rich and their food is choice.
verses.17: Should they, then, empty their net and never cease to slaughter nations without mercy?

notes:
Notes  
- v. 10: "heaps up dust" renders the Hebrew "יִצְבֹּר עָפָר" — the verb "to heap up" and the noun "dust" are literal.  
- v. 11: "their might is their god" translates "זֹאת כֹּחוֹ לֵאלֹהֽוֹ" — the phrase is metaphorical, referring to their power as their deity.  
- v. 13: "your eyes are too pure to look on evil" renders "טְהוֹר עֵינַיִם מֵרְאוֹת רָע" — the construction is idiomatic, meaning "pure of eye" in the sense of moral clarity.  
- v. 15: "in a hook" and "in a net" reflect the Hebrew "בְּחַכָּה" and "בְּמִכְמַרְתּוֹ", respectively — both are literal terms for fishing gear.  
- v. 17: "empty their net" translates "הַעַל כֵּן יָרִיק חֶרְמוֹ" — the verb "to empty" and noun "net" are standard.
